label: copy-phase input w fed back as the 2nd-4th original token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input is the letter w (in_tok == w carries ~100% of activation mass). It is concentrated early in the copy: recall_idx 2 and 3 (w was original token 1 or 2) hold ~94% of mass and are the strongest (top examples are all w at original position 1, ~0.95 of max); recall_idx 4 (w at original position 3) fires weakly and only about half the time, more reliably for longer sequences with outputs remaining. Essentially silent for w input in the original phase, at recall_idx 1 (w as the first original token being fed back) and at recall_idx >= 5; never fires on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the original phase. Not modulated by out_tok, prev_tok, or digits.

issues: The original predicate misses a systematic gap: the feature never fires on the final copy step (to_go == 0), whatever recall_idx is. On dev, with in_tok == w and to_go == 0, precision is 0.0 at recall_idx 2 (n=468), 3 (n=2426) and 4 (n=2692). The predicate counts all of these as positives, and they make up most of its false positives (about 5.6k of the 11k).

The explanation says to_go only matters at recall_idx 4 ('more reliably when more outputs remain'). That is wrong: the dependence holds across the board. At recall_idx 2 precision is 0.00 at to_go 0, 0.36 at to_go 1 (mass 0.3%), and 1.00 at to_go >= 2. At recall_idx 3 it is 0.00 at to_go 0 and 0.99-1.00 at to_go >= 1. At recall_idx 4 it is 0.00, 0.29, 0.72, 0.81 and 0.77 for to_go 0 through 4.

As a result, the feature is essentially silent for L = 4. At recall_idx 3 with L == 4, precision is 0.0. At recall_idx 2 with L == 4, precision is 0.36 with only 0.3% of the mass. The explanation's claim that recall_idx 2 and 3 are 'the strongest' cases does not hold when they fall on the last or second-to-last step.

Claims that check out: all activation mass is in the copy phase (phase 2) with in_tok == w. It is silent in the original and delimiter phases. recall_idx 1 is near-silent (precision 0.025, mass 0.1%) and recall_idx >= 5 is near-silent. out_tok and prev_tok are flat. The original predicate reproduces on dev: P 0.764, R 0.982, F1 0.859, mass recall 0.998.
Remaining false positives under the improved predicate are mostly at recall_idx 3-4 in sequences that contain a second w later on. This is minor, not a major class.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input w fed back as original token 1-3 (recall_idx 2-4), but not on the last copy step(s)

final_label: copy-phase input w fed back as original token 1-3 (recall_idx 2-4), but not on the last copy step(s)
